clue.text: It requires courage to have one - rather than love!

definitions.text: It requires courage to have one - rather than love!

blocks.clueFragment: It requires courage to have one
blocks.note: surface reading: a daring act or bold confrontation that takes nerve
setter's reading: the opposite of making love, as in the slogan about making love instead of war

explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes the slogan 'make love, not war': what you have instead of love is armed combat, the theme word every other clue refers to as 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight between armies takes bravery, and it is the warlike alternative the peace slogan contrasts with love.

clue.text: British left to confess what ships were at 28

blocks.note: the abbreviation for British
the abbreviation for left
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: The British were left to admit the fate of their ships in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: At Taranto (28 across) in 1940 British aircraft sank or wrecked Italian battleships.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpedoed Italian battleships were destroyed by explosions, so they were wrecked in that blasting sense.

clue.text: Rose to power in 1 across

blocks.note: surface reading: someone climbed to authority
setter's reading: the flower emblem of the dynasty Henry VII founded after winning Bosworth in 1485

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as a verb, but it is also the heraldic flower; Henry VII took the throne by battle at Bosworth and made that rose his badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal house founded by Henry VII gained the crown through victory at Bosworth and adopted a red-and-white rose emblem.

clue.text: House for 2?

blocks.note: surface reading: a home built for a couple
setter's reading: a royal dynasty, the line the 2 down founder claimed descent through

explanation.walkthrough: '2' is 2 down, and 'House' means a royal family; Henry Tudor's claim came through the red-rose line of the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII inherited his royal claim through his mother from the dynasty descended from John of Gaunt.

clue.text: Criticise one stroke in Mogul 1 across

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
the Roman numeral for one
a pat is a light stroke

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a Mughal emperor's battle record, faulting a single move.
explanation.definitionFit: The first battle fought at this Indian town in 1526 founded Babur's Mughal empire, hence a Mogul fight.

clue.text: Like logs pruned by 1st and 2nd of the Muses

indicators.note: pruning cuts parts away, so the named letters are removed from the front

blocks.note: natural logarithms are called Napierian, after the mathematician John Napier
the first two letters of that word

explanation.surface: Wood gets trimmed by the first and second of the nine Muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Logs' are logarithms, not timber. Pieria was the Muses' home, hence Pope's 'Pierian spring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieria in Macedonia was sacred to the nine goddesses of the arts, so the adjective refers to them and to poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Customary for no vermin to be docked

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
mice are vermin

explanation.surface: It is usual practice to cut the tails off vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: Docked means losing a tail, and here the mice lose their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomic is a rare word meaning conventional or habitual, from the Greek nomos, custom or law.

clue.text: BUPA's rule for treatment can be followed

indicators.note: something sent for treatment is worked on and altered, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A private health insurer's policy on treatment is easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: BUPA is a large British private health insurer, so 'treatment' sounds medical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pursuable is able to be chased or carried on, which is what being followed means.

clue.text: Three bridges at what should see an end to 1 acrosses

definitions.text: what should see an end to 1 acrosses

indicators.note: a bridge spans a gap, so the three is split to sit around the other piece

blocks.note: a trey is the three in cards or dice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Three bridges at the place where fighting ought to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: TRE(AT)Y. A trey is the card or die face showing three.
explanation.definitionFit: A signed peace agreement between warring states is meant to end their fighting.

clue.text: Confer gold on reported victor of 29

indicators.note: reported means told aloud, so the word that follows is wanted for its sound

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the Vikings who won at Maldon (29 across) were Danes

explanation.surface: Bestow gold on the man said to have won a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is 29 across, Maldon, won by Danish raiders in 991.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to confer holy orders on someone, granting them priestly status.

clue.text: 1 across where French retreating ran into foul deed

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the following word is read in reverse
something foul is messed up, so the letters of the next word get rearranged
one piece goes into the middle of the jumbled letters that follow

blocks.note: the French word for where is ou
the letters of deed, rearranged
taken as written, then turned backwards

explanation.surface: French soldiers falling back rush into some wicked act.
explanation.walkthrough: OU + DE(NAR)DE: Marlborough beat the French at Oudenarde in 1708, so the retreating French suit the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Oudenarde, in Flanders, was the scene of Marlborough's 1708 victory over the French army.

clue.text: West sees service in 1 across

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the service goes within the West

blocks.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress
the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone in the west of the country does military service at a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: MA(RN)E. The West is the actress Mae West, not a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Marne in France gave its name to two major First World War engagements, in 1914 and 1918.

clue.text: Originally, not a Russian victory at 1 across

indicators.note: originally points to the beginnings, so each following word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: History notes that a certain battle was no win for the Russians.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Charles XII of Sweden crushed Peter the Great's army at Narva in 1700.
explanation.definitionFit: Narva, in Estonia, was where the Swedish army routed a much larger Russian force in 1700.

clue.text: 1 across for a gin palace

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a royal court is a palace, as in Hampton Court

explanation.surface: A historic battle compared to a Victorian gin palace, a flashy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin palace was a gaudy Victorian public house; here it splits into its words and the palace becomes a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt, in northern France, was where Henry V's English archers defeated the French in 1415.

clue.text: 1 across continued verbally

indicators.note: verbally means in speech, so what is wanted is how the phrase sounds when said

blocks.note: to press on is to continue, and the past tense spoken quickly matches the town

explanation.surface: A battle that just kept going, as described in words.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston, a Lancashire town, saw battles in 1648 and 1715; said aloud it is 'pressed on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston in Lancashire was the site of Cromwell's 1648 victory and the Jacobite defeat of 1715.

clue.text: One downing spirits or one cutting out

blocks.note: taken as written
to excise is to cut out

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker of spirits, or a surgeon who removes tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a double definition, but 'or' is a word to place, with no signal for the placing. 'Downing spirits' suggests drinking; here it means defeating ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who casts out demons or ghosts overcomes evil spirits, putting them down.

clue.text: North Sea runs close to 1 across

indicators.note: colours that run spread and mix, so the letters of the sea move about

blocks.note: the abbreviation for north
the letters of sea, rearranged
by means near or close to

explanation.surface: The North Sea flows near the site of a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Sea' reads as one place name, but it splits into a compass point and a word to jumble. Naseby is in Northamptonshire, nowhere near the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseby, in Northamptonshire, saw the decisive Parliamentarian victory of the English Civil War in 1645.

clue.text: Foundations set up by imaginative studies on vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it, so the pieces read from bottom to top

blocks.note: by the door means at the door
the arts, as opposed to the sciences
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Building foundations put in place by creative study done on board a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Substrata are underlying layers on which other things rest, the base or groundwork beneath.

clue.text: 1 across in second addressed for poet in first

indicators.note: to address someone is to speak to them, so the words are to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: a letter for someone is addressed to them, and Rupert Brooke was a poet of the First World War

explanation.surface: A battle of one war, and a letter sent to a poet of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' and 'first' are the two World Wars. A letter addressed to the poet Rupert Brooke, who died in 1915, would read 'To Brooke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobruk, a Libyan port, was besieged and fought over repeatedly in the North African campaign of the Second World War.

clue.text: Tokyo's excited about races for goddess

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the city's letters are stirred into a new order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the races

blocks.note: the letters of the city, rearranged
the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: People in Tokyo get worked up over racing.
explanation.walkthrough: KOTY(TT)O. The TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: Kotytto, or Cotys, was a Thracian goddess worshipped with orgiastic rites, later adopted in Greece.

clue.text: Au fait with Beresford's first real controversial 1 across

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the commander's name
something controversial is disputed and stirred up, so the gathered letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the general's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone well informed about General Beresford's genuinely disputed battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Au' from 'Au fait' joins the fodder; the rest is surface. Beresford's 1811 win at Albuera was famously costly and its handling disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Albuera, in Spain, was where Beresford's Anglo-Allied army fought Soult's French troops in the Peninsular War.

clue.text: Transmitter raises atmosphere in field

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other, so the atmosphere sits inside the field
in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or field
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A broadcasting mast lifts the mood across the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: L(AIR)EA, then turned upwards. Atmosphere looks like mood here.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is the rod or wire that sends out or picks up radio signals.

clue.text: Goals or a near miss cited by poor loser

indicators.note: cited by means quoted within the words given, so the letters run across them

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the fourth

explanation.surface: A beaten competitor points to goals and near misses as excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or contestant that finished outside the places, an unsuccessful competitor.

clue.text: Creative traits make one?

indicators.note: making something out of material reshapes it, so these letters are rebuilt into a new word

blocks.note: the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether imaginative characteristics are what make a person a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A creative, used as a noun, is a person who works in the arts, such as a painter.

clue.text: Run out to shout approval about way Odo was caught in this 1 across

definitions.text: Odo was caught in this 1 across

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shout of approval wraps around the way

blocks.note: the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a batsman dismissed run out
a cheer is a shout of approval
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A dismissed batsman is cheered while a bishop named Odo is captured in a siege.
explanation.walkthrough: RO + CHE(ST)ER. Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother, was besieged and taken at Rochester in 1088.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester Castle in Kent was besieged in 1088, and the rebel Bishop Odo surrendered there.

clue.text: Where to eat in Germany?

blocks.note: surface reading: asking for a good restaurant in Germany
setter's reading: the German verb meaning to eat, which is also a city in the Ruhr

explanation.walkthrough: The German infinitive for eating is also the name of a Ruhr industrial city, so the place is answered by the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a large Ruhr city, and the identically spelt German verb means to eat.

clue.text: Excursions by Arabs halted at 1 across

blocks.note: first meaning: trips or outings
second meaning: the battle in France where the Umayyad advance was stopped in 732

explanation.surface: Arab travellers stopping on their trips to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Trips and outings are tours, and the French city of Tours names the 732 battle where Charles Martel stopped the Umayyad army.

clue.text: Driven to be purified from the head down

indicators.note: the head is the top of a down entry, and taking it off removes the first letter

blocks.note: purged means cleansed or purified

explanation.surface: Someone was pushed into cleansing from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being urged means being pushed or impelled to act, the sense of being driven to do something.

clue.text: 1 across concerns snuffing out the East

indicators.note: snuffing out a candle extinguishes it, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: issues are concerns or matters of worry
the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A battle concerned with crushing Eastern power.
explanation.walkthrough: ISSUES loses an E. Fittingly, Issus is where Alexander the Great beat the Persian king Darius in 333 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Issus, in south-east Anatolia, was where Alexander the Great defeated Darius III of Persia.

clue.text: Victory in this 1 across

blocks.note: surface reading: a battle that ended in a win
setter's reading: HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship, which fought in a famous 1805 sea battle

explanation.walkthrough: Victory reads as a win, but it is the name of Nelson's flagship; the battle it fought in is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson sailed HMS Victory at the 1805 battle off Cape Trafalgar, where the British fleet beat the French and Spanish.

clue.text: Part-timers were sufficient for 1 across

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve
funds that ran to something were enough to cover it

explanation.surface: Reservists proved enough to win a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the Territorial Army, the British army's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Taranto, in southern Italy, was where British carrier aircraft crippled the Italian fleet at anchor in 1940.

clue.text: Crew taking on old irregular in this 1 across

indicators.note: irregular means out of the normal order, so these letters are scrambled
taking on means taking aboard, so the crew holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: to man a ship is to crew it
the letters of old, rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's crew takes on an old irregular soldier for a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: MA(LDO)N. 'Crew' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Maldon in Essex was where Viking raiders defeated the English under Byrhtnoth in 991, recorded in an Old English poem.
